prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` now loads it. The full test suite passes, including 13 new tests; flake8 isn't installed here, so I didn't run the style check. List items starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` plus a space get a checkbox, which is `checked` for x/X and `disabled` unless `clickable=True`. The `<li>` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`; an empty string means no class). This works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists, and inline markup after the marker is kept. The marker is matched in the raw text before inline processing, so it still works when a `[x]: url` link definition exists, and `\[x]` stays plain text. One space is kept between the checkbox and the item text. I also added the docs page, the API reference page, the extension index and mkdocs nav entries, and a changelog entry under a new `[unreleased]` section.
